questions.question: The lengths of the diagonals of a rhombus compare as 3 times some value to 4 times that same value. If the area of the rhombus is 216 cm², what are the actual lengths of the two diagonals?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of diagonals d₁ : d₂ = 3 : 4

Area = 1/2 × (Product of ratio parts) × x²

216 = 1/2 × 3 × 4 × x² ⇒ 216 = 6x²

x² = 36 ⇒ x = 6

Actual diagonals = 3 × 6 and 4 × 6 = 18 cm and 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm and 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of diagonals = 3 : 4, Area of rhombus = 216 cm².

**Formula Used:** Area of Rhombus = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d4185ae34bb1acf87843d553473cb5a4cf84a4b323fe6fbc295b60d0f3dd864.png] 

⇒ Let the lengths of the diagonals be 3x and 4x.

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 3x × 4x

⇒ 216 = 6x²

⇒ x² = 216 ÷ 6

⇒ x² = 36

⇒ x = √36 = 6

⇒ First diagonal (d₁) = 3 × 6 = 18 cm

⇒ Second diagonal (d₂) = 4 × 6 = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm and 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rhombus

A rhombus is a quadrilateral with all four sides equal. Opposite angles are equal and adjacent angles are supplementary (sum to 180°).

Diagonal Property

The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles (90°).

Side-Diagonal Relation

If side is 'a' and diagonals are d₁ and d₂, then 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

Perimeter of Rhombus

The perimeter is calculated as 4 × side.</p

questions.question: Two right prisms have the same height, but their bases are triangles with areas in the ratio 3:5. What is the ratio of their volumes?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ **Volume of a right prism** = **Base Area** × **Height**. Since both prisms have the **same height**, the **Volume** is **directly proportional** to the **Base Area**. Ratio of Volumes = Ratio of Base Areas. Given Base Area Ratio = 3 : 5. **∴ The correct answer is 3:5.**

questions.question: A right circular cylinder has height 20 cm and curved surface area 880 cm². What is its volume? (use π=22/7)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Radius r = CSA ÷ (2 × π × h)

r = 880 ÷ (2 × 22/7 × 20) = 7 cm

Volume V = (CSA × r) ÷ 2

V = (880 × 7) ÷ 2 = 440 × 7 = 3080 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 3080 cm³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height (h) = 20 cm

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 880 cm²

π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

CSA of cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5abe150ca48ed3172cb2276c8f510baf53fe82c332f5777bb5835253198bc56b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 880 = 2 × (22/7) × r × 20

⇒ 880 = (880/7) × r

⇒ r = 7 cm

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 7 × 7 × 20

⇒ Volume = 154 × 20

⇒ Volume = 3080 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 3080 cm³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The total surface area of a cylinder includes the curved surface and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same radius and height as a cylinder has exactly 1/3 the volume of the cylinder: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Base Area

The area of the circular base (or top) of the cylinder is given by the formula: Area = πr².</p

questions.question: Find the value of: (sqrt{625} - sqrt{81}) times (sqrt{49} + sqrt{121})
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly substitute the **square roots**: (25 − 9) × (7 + 11)

⇒ 16 × 18

Apply the **middle-term square trick**: 17² − 1 = 289 − 1 = 288.

**∴ The correct answer is 288.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (√625 − √81) × (√49 + √121)

**Formula Used:** **BODMAS** (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ √625 = 25

⇒ √81 = 9

⇒ √49 = 7

⇒ √121 = 11

⇒ (25 − 9) × (7 + 11)

⇒ 16 × 18

⇒ 288

**∴ The correct answer is 288.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Squares Table

Memorizing squares up to 30 is essential for **banking exams**. Key values: 25² = 625, 11² = 121, 9² = 81, and 7² = 49.

BODMAS Rule

Operations inside **brackets** must be completed before performing multiplication outside the brackets.

Algebraic Identity for Multiplication

The product of two numbers (x − a) and (x + a) is always x² − a². Here, 16 × 18 = (17 − 1)(17 + 1) = 17² − 1².</p

questions.question: Let a = 2⁴ · 3² · 5 and b = 2² · 3 · 7³. which of the following is true?

options.text: L.C.M(a, b) × GCD(a, b) = a + b

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**LCM** is the product of the **highest powers** of all prime factors present in the numbers.

Highest powers: 2 → 2⁴, 3 → 3², 5 → 5¹, 7 → 7³.

**LCM(a, b)** = 2⁴ × 3² × 5 × 7³.

**GCD** is the product of the **lowest powers** of common prime factors: 2² × 3.

Comparing with options, only the first statement matches the calculated **LCM**.

**∴ The correct answer is L.C.M(a, b) = 2⁴ × 3² × 5 × 7³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a = 2⁴ × 3² × 5

b = 2² × 3 × 7³

**Formula Used:**

**LCM (Least Common Multiple)** = Product of the highest power of each prime factor involved in the numbers.

**GCD (Greatest Common Divisor)** = Product of the lowest power of each common prime factor.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factors involved in both numbers are **2, 3, 5, and 7**.

⇒ For **LCM**, we take the maximum exponent for each prime:

⇒ Max power of 2 = 2⁴

⇒ Max power of 3 = 3²

⇒ Max power of 5 = 5¹

⇒ Max power of 7 = 7³

⇒ **LCM(a, b)** = 2⁴ × 3² × 5 × 7³

⇒ For **GCD**, we take the minimum exponent for each common prime:

⇒ Min power of 2 = 2²

⇒ Min power of 3 = 3¹

⇒ **GCD(a, b)** = 2² × 3 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is L.C.M(a, b) = 2⁴ × 3² × 5 × 7³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between LCM and GCD

For any two positive integers x and y, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **LCM** and **GCD**: x × y = LCM(x, y) × GCD(x, y).

GCD of Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers have no common prime factors, their **GCD** is 1, and they are called **co-prime** or relatively prime numbers.

Prime Factorization Method

This method expresses each number as a product of **prime powers**, making it easy to identify the highest and lowest powers for **LCM** and **GCD** respectively.

questions.question: An online seller purchases a laptop at ₹40,000. He lists it at a 25% markup. Due to a festive sale, he gives a flat 10% discount on the listed price and offers free shipping costing him ₹500. What is the net profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective Selling Price factor = 1.25 (Markup) × 0.90 (Discount) = 1.125

Selling Price (SP) = 40,000 × 1.125 = ₹45,000

Total effective Cost Price (CP) = 40,000 + 500 (Shipping) = ₹40,500

Net Profit % = [(45,000 − 40,500) ÷ 40,500] × 100 = (4,500 ÷ 40,500) × 100 = 1/9 × 100 = 11.11%

**∴ The correct answer is 11.11%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Purchase Price (CP) = ₹40,000

Markup Percentage = 25%

Discount Percentage = 10%

Shipping Cost = ₹500

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ac76df8312d4201a73d5cc3d9c5ee0332dfcb729f1f99b82156b2aaa516b24dc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = CP + 25% of CP

⇒ MP = 40,000 + (0.25 × 40,000) = 40,000 + 10,000 = ₹50,000

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − 10% of MP

⇒ SP = 50,000 − (0.10 × 50,000) = 50,000 − 5,000 = ₹45,000

⇒ Total effective cost for seller = Purchase Price + Shipping

⇒ Total CP = 40,000 + 500 = ₹40,500

⇒ Net Profit = SP − Total CP = 45,000 − 40,500 = ₹4,500

⇒ Net Profit % = (Net Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

⇒ Net Profit % = (4,500 ÷ 40,500) × 100 = 1/9 × 100 = 11.11%

**∴ The correct answer is 11.11%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Markup and Discount Relation

The relationship between CP and MP is given by: MP/CP = (100 + Profit%)/(100 − Discount%).

Overhead Charges

Any extra expenses like **transportation, repairs, or taxes** incurred after purchase are always added to the initial Cost Price to calculate the total effective Cost Price.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value is increased by x% and then decreased by y%, the net change is [x − y − (xy/100)]%.

questions.question: A and B together can complete a piece of work in 10 days. B alone can complete it in 15 days. In how many days can A alone complete the work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by **A** alone = (Product of days) ÷ (Difference of days)

Time = (10 × 15) ÷ (15 − 10)

Time = 150 ÷ 5 = **30 days**

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (**A + B**) = **10 days**

Time taken by **B** alone = **15 days**

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = **LCM** of time taken

Efficiency = **Total Work** ÷ **Time**

Efficiency of **A** = Efficiency of (**A + B**) − Efficiency of **B**

⇒ Efficiency of **A** = 3 − 2 = **1 unit/day**

⇒ Time taken by **A** alone = **Total Work** ÷ **Efficiency of A**

⇒ Time taken by **A** = 30 ÷ 1 = **30 days**

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency Relation

Work = Time × Efficiency. For a constant amount of work, time is inversely proportional to efficiency.

Combined Work Formula

If **A** takes **x** days and **B** takes **y** days, together they take (**x × y**) ÷ (**x + y**) days.

One Day Work Concept

If a person completes a piece of work in **n** days, then the work done by that person in 1 day is **1/n**.</p

questions.question: If sec theta + tan theta = p , what is the value of sec theta in terms of p?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the identity sec² θ − tan² θ = 1.

If sec θ + tan θ = p, then sec θ − tan θ = 1/p.

Adding both equations: (sec θ + tan θ) + (sec θ − tan θ) = p + 1/p.

2 sec θ = (p² + 1)/p ⇒ sec θ = (p² + 1)/2p.

**∴ The correct answer is (p² + 1)/2p.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** sec θ + tan θ = p --- (i)

**Formula Used:** sec² θ − tan² θ = 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5fd89b0de908e55a9a35d4729e26673564601e59a80de63da74a28ef9e13b05c.png] 

⇒ We know that (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = 1

⇒ Substituting (i): p × (sec θ − tan θ) = 1

⇒ sec θ − tan θ = 1/p --- (ii)

⇒ Adding equation (i) and (ii):

⇒ (sec θ + tan θ) + (sec θ − tan θ) = p + 1/p

⇒ 2 sec θ = (p² + 1)/p

⇒ sec θ = (p² + 1)/2p

**∴ The correct answer is (p² + 1)/2p.**

**__Additional Information__**

Value of tan θ

If sec θ + tan θ = p, then by subtracting the equations we get tan θ = (p² − 1)/2p.

Cosecant and Cotangent Identity

Similar to sec-tan, cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1. If cosec θ + cot θ = k, then cosec θ = (k² + 1)/2k.

Pythagorean Triplets

For any value p, the expressions (p² − 1), 2p, and (p² + 1) always form a Pythagorean triplet.</p

questions.question: If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume values for a, b, and c such that their sum is 0.

Let a = 1, b = 1, and c = −2, then a + b + c = 1 + 1 + (−2) = 0.

Now, calculate a³ + b³ + c³ = 1³ + 1³ + (−2)³ = 1 + 1 − 8 = −6.

Check the options: 3abc = 3 × 1 × 1 × (−2) = −6.

**∴ The correct answer is 3abc.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** a + b + c = 0

**Formula Used:** a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (0) × (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = 0

⇒ a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

**∴ The correct answer is 3abc.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity

The expression a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc is a standard cubic identity used to factorize polynomials.

Special Case for 3abc

The condition a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc is satisfied if either a + b + c = 0 or a = b = c.

Square Expansion

The term (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca) can be rewritten as 1/2[(a−b)² + (b−c)² + (c−a)²].

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest and simple interest on ₹10,000 for 2 years at 5% per annum is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For 2 years, the difference between **Compound Interest** and **Simple Interest** is given by:

Difference = P × (R/100)²

⇒ Difference = 10,000 × (5/100) × (5/100)

⇒ Difference = 10,000 × (25/10,000)

⇒ Difference = ₹25

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Principal (P)** = ₹10,000, **Rate (R)** = 5% per annum, **Time (T)** = 2 years.

Formula: **SI** = (P × R × T) / 100 | **CI** = P[(1 + R/100)T − 1]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8254e3d6ced6a4fca18ca6cee9d6396c98a29425333110a7ea0f30d0f2074a21.png] 

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI)** = (10,000 × 5 × 2) / 100 = ₹1,000

⇒ **Compound Interest (CI)** = 10,000 × [(1 + 5/100)² − 1]

⇒ CI = 10,000 × [(21/20)² − 1] = 10,000 × [441/400 − 1]

⇒ CI = 10,000 × (41/400) = 25 × 41 = ₹1,025

⇒ Difference = CI − SI = 1,025 − 1,000 = ₹25

**∴ The correct answer is ₹25.**

**__Additional Information__**

Difference for 3 years

The difference between CI and SI for 3 years is calculated as P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Effective Rate Method

For 2 years at R%, the effective CI rate is (2R + R²/100)%. The difference from SI (2R%) is exactly R²/100%.

First Year Interest

When interest is compounded annually, the **Simple Interest** and **Compound Interest** for the first year are always equal.

questions.question: If ₹12,000 is deposited in a simple interest account that yields 10% annually, what will be the interest earned after two and a half years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Effective rate** of interest = Rate × Time

Effective rate = 10% × 2.5 = 25%

Interest = 25% of **Principal** = 25% of ₹12,000

Interest = 12,000 ÷ 4 = 3,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal** (P) = ₹12,000

**Rate** (R) = 10% per annum

**Time** (T) = 2.5 years

**Formula Used:**

**Simple Interest** (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b692818a6756071ca614f34563209c898f31b845195bd15ddd6a5a1a32aec5e1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (12000 × 10 × 2.5) / 100

⇒ SI = 120 × 10 × 2.5

⇒ SI = 1200 × 2.5

⇒ SI = 3000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Calculation

The **Total Amount** (A) is the sum of the principal and the interest earned: A = P + SI. In this case, A = 12,000 + 3,000 = ₹15,000.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In **Simple Interest**, the principal remains constant for the entire duration. In **Compound Interest**, the interest from previous periods is added to the principal for the next calculation.

Time Conversion

Always ensure **Time** (T) is in years when the **Rate** (R) is per annum. For example, 6 months should be used as 0.5 years in the formula.

questions.question: A trader sells two items. On the first item, he makes a profit of 15%, and on the second item, he incurs a loss of 10%. If the selling price of both items is the same (₹3450 each), what is his overall profit or loss percentage on the entire transaction?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Item 1 (15% Profit): 15% = 3/20 ⇒ **CP : SP** = 20 : 23

Item 2 (10% Loss): 10% = 1/10 ⇒ **CP : SP** = 10 : 9

Equating SP (LCM of 23, 9 = 207):

Item 1: (20 : 23) × 9 = 180 : 207 | Item 2: (10 : 9) × 23 = 230 : 207

Total CP = 180 + 230 = 410 | Total SP = 207 + 207 = 414

Overall Profit % = (4 / 410) × 100 = 40/41 ≈ 0.98% profit

**∴ The correct answer is 0.98% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Selling Price (SP) of both items = ₹3450 each. Profit on item 1 = 15%. Loss on item 2 = 10%.

**Formula:** Cost Price (CP) = SP × [100 / (100 ± Profit/Loss %)]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e99be45064abc5dab631f5c0ababa886fb49152cd032c8d463016578b221b57d.png] 

⇒ CP₁ = 3450 × (100 / 115) = 30 × 100 = ₹3000

⇒ CP₂ = 3450 × (100 / 90) = 34500 / 9 = ₹3833.33

⇒ Total CP = 3000 + 3833.33 = ₹6833.33

⇒ Total SP = 3450 + 3450 = ₹6900

⇒ Total Profit = 6900 − 6833.33 = ₹66.67

⇒ Profit % = (66.67 / 6833.33) × 100 ≈ 0.9756%

⇒ Overall Profit % ≈ 0.98%

**∴ The correct answer is 0.98% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Same SP and Equal Profit/Loss Percentage

When two articles are sold at the same price, one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%, there is always an overall loss given by (x/10)² %.

Successive Percentage Change

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the effective change is [a + b + (ab/100)]%. This is useful for successive discounts or population growth.

Marked Price and Discount Relation

The ratio of CP to MP is given by CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%). This helps solve problems involving markups and discounts directly.

questions.question: Consider two points on the ground, at distances a and b from the base of a tower (a > b) from the foot of the tower and in the same straight line with it are 30° and 60° respectively. The height of the tower is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the angles of elevation from two points at distances **a** and **b** from the base are **complementary** (sum = 90°), the height **h** is always the **geometric mean** of the distances.

Given angles: 30° and 60° ⇒ Sum = 30° + 60° = 90°.

Since the angles are complementary, **h = √(a × b)**.

**∴ The correct answer is √ab.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of first point from base = **a**

Distance of second point from base = **b**

Angles of elevation = **30°** and **60°**

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular / Base = **Height / Distance**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a40050b056356e5817e4a128435211901c985376834469efd146071514105f04.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the height of the tower be **h**.

⇒ In the larger triangle (distance a):

⇒ tan 30° = h / a

⇒ 1 / √3 = h / a

⇒ **h = a / √3** --- (Equation 1)

⇒ In the smaller triangle (distance b):

⇒ tan 60° = h / b

⇒ √3 = h / b

⇒ **h = b × √3** --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Multiplying Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ h × h = (a / √3) × (b × √3)

⇒ h² = a × b

⇒ **h = √ab**

**∴ The correct answer is √ab.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles Property

When the angles of elevation from two points are θ and (90° − θ), the height of the object is the geometric mean of the distances: h = √(d₁ × d₂).

Trigonometric Ratios

Standard values for height and distance problems: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Angle-Distance Relationship

As an observer moves **closer** to the foot of a tower, the angle of elevation **increases**. Hence, the point at distance 'b' (smaller distance) has the larger angle (60°).</p

questions.question: The square root of 7 + 4sqrt{3} is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Compare 7 + 4√3 with the identity a² + b² + 2ab.

Here, 2ab = 4√3 ⇒ ab = 2√3.

Find factors of 2√3 whose squares sum to 7: 2 and √3.

Check: 2² + (√3)² = 4 + 3 = 7.

The square root is (a + b) = 2 + √3.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 + √3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 7 + 4√3

**Formula Used:** (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f5e777ce80b01d01832e41dfc640e4f64a5883f927af3c1bd5a77e1b6b5996f.png] 

⇒ 7 + 4√3 = 4 + 3 + 4√3

⇒ 7 + 4√3 = 2² + (√3)² + 2 × 2 × √3

⇒ 7 + 4√3 = (2 + √3)²

⇒ √(7 + 4√3) = √(2 + √3)²

⇒ √(7 + 4√3) = 2 + √3

**∴ The correct answer is 2 + √3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Negative Surds

For an expression a − 2√b, the square root is √x − √y where x + y = a and xy = b.

Rationalization of Surds

To rationalize 1/(a + √b), multiply the numerator and denominator by its conjugate (a − √b).

Pure and Mixed Surds

A surd consisting of only an irrational part is a pure surd (e.g., √3), while one with a rational part is a mixed surd (e.g., 2 + √3).

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B. Together they finish a work in 12 days. How long would B take alone?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio **A : B = 2 : 1**.

Combined efficiency = 2 + 1 = **3 units/day**.

Total work = Combined efficiency × Total days = 3 × 12 = **36 units**.

Time for **B alone** = Total work ÷ B's efficiency = 36 ÷ 1 = **36 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Efficiency of **A** = 2 × Efficiency of **B**

Time taken by (**A + B**) together = 12 days

**Formula Used:**

**Total Work = Efficiency × Time**

Combined efficiency of **A + B** = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day

⇒ Let efficiency of **B** = 1 unit/day.

⇒ Efficiency of **A** = 2 × 1 = 2 units/day.

⇒ **Total Work** = Combined Efficiency × Time = 3 × 12 = 36 units.

⇒ Time taken by **B alone** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B = 36 ÷ 1 = 36 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete a task. If the ratio of efficiencies of two people is x : y, the ratio of time taken by them will be y : x.

Combined Work Formula

If person A takes 'a' days and person B takes 'b' days, then together they will take (a × b) ÷ (a + b) days to complete the work.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the **ratio of work done** by each person, which is equivalent to the ratio of their efficiencies if they work for the same amount of time.</p

questions.question: A train moving at a speed of 126 km/h crosses a bridge of length 250 meters in 50 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Speed in m/s = 126 × 5/18 = 35 m/s.

Total distance (Train + Bridge) = Speed × Time = 35 × 50 = 1750 m.

Length of train = Total distance − Bridge length = 1750 − 250 = 1500 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 1500 meters.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of train = 126 km/h

Length of bridge = 250 m

Time taken = 50 s

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Total Distance = Length of Train + Length of Bridge

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ba0aa1c32d4ae067987beb7e636fb2ade2b50120feb15f61ba47b72dceea6459.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed in m/s = 126 × (5/18)

⇒ Speed = 7 × 5 = 35 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = 35 × 50

⇒ Train Length + 250 = 1750

⇒ Train Length = 1750 − 250

⇒ Train Length = 1500 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1500 meters.**

**__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Distance Logic

When a train crosses a point object (pole, man), distance = train length. When it crosses a platform or bridge, distance = train length + object length.

Relative Speed

If two trains move in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: The radii of two concentric circles with centre 'O' is 12 cm and 18 cm, respectively. AB is a chord on the larger circle that is tangent to the smaller circle making contact at point 'C'. If AD is a diameter of the larger circle, then find the length of CD.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In triangle ABD, C and O are midpoints of AB and AD respectively.

By Midpoint Theorem: BD = 2 × OC = 2 × 12 = 24 cm.

In right triangle ABC: BC² = R² − r² = 18² − 12² = 180.

Since angle ABD = 90°, in triangle CBD: CD² = BC² + BD².

Calculation: CD² = 180 + 24² = 180 + 576 = 756.

**∴ The correct answer is √756 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of smaller circle (r) = 12 cm

Radius of larger circle (R) = 18 cm

AD is the diameter of the larger circle.

**Formula Used:**

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

Midpoint Theorem: Segment joining midpoints of two sides is half the third side.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/27249ca62b889f61f9bc0b84bb283b23f5c24aad13d29b6a1d030dca907db7fd.png] 
⇒ OC = 12 cm, OA = 18 cm
⇒ In right triangle OCA, AC² = OA² − OC² = 18² − 12² = 180
⇒ BC = AC = √180 cm (Radius from center bisects the chord)
⇒ In triangle ABD, O is the midpoint of diameter AD and C is the midpoint of chord AB
⇒ By Midpoint Theorem, BD = 2 × OC = 2 × 12 = 24 cm
⇒ Angle ABD = 90° (Angle in a semicircle)
⇒ In right triangle CBD, CD² = BC² + BD² = 180 + 24²
⇒ CD² = 180 + 576 = 756
⇒ CD = √756 cm

**∴ The correct answer is √756 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Radius-Tangent Property

The radius of a circle is always perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact (Angle = 90°).

Midpoint Theorem

The line segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and equal to half of its length.

Angle in a Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of the circle is always a right angle (90°).</p

questions.question: The distance between the centres of the two circles is 73 cm, and the radii of the circles are 29 cm and 19 cm. Find the length of the transverse common tangent drawn to the two circles.
questions.solution:
"
 * *Wait, I've spent too much time checking constraints. I will proceed with the generation.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Length of **Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)** = √(d² − (r₁ + r₂)²)

Sum of radii = 29 + 19 = 48 cm

TCT = √(73² − 48²)

Using a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b):

TCT = √((73 − 48) × (73 + 48)) = √(25 × 121) = 5 × 11 = 55 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 55 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between centres (d) = 73 cm

Radius of first circle (r₁) = 29 cm

Radius of second circle (r₂) = 19 cm

**Formula Used:**

Length of Transverse Common Tangent = √[(Distance between centres)² − (r₁ + r₂)²]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d72a5f644f40b8ef228bee937567c4926870e668bd105fcec6cd4f1c5e91900e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of radii = r₁ + r₂ = 29 + 19 = 48 cm

⇒ Length of TCT = √(73² − 48²)

⇒ Length of TCT = √(5329 − 2304)

⇒ Length of TCT = √3025

⇒ Length of TCT = 55 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 55 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

The length of the direct common tangent is given by √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²).

Number of Common Tangents

If d > r₁ + r₂, there are 4 common tangents (2 direct, 2 transverse). If d = r₁ + r₂, there are 3 common tangents.

Pythagorean Triplet

The numbers (48, 55, 73) form a Pythagorean triplet since 48² + 55² = 2304 + 3025 = 5329 = 73².</p

questions.question: If 13A = 12B and 14B = 15C, then find A:C.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given 13A = 12B and 14B = 15C.

Ratios are A/B = 12/13 and B/C = 15/14.

To find A:C, multiply the ratios: A/C = (A/B) × (B/C).

A/C = (12/13) × (15/14) = 180/182.

Simplify by 2: A/C = 90/91.

**∴ The correct answer is 90:91.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

13A = 12B

14B = 15C

**Formula Used:**

A/C = (A/B) × (B/C)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/199f0cf2c9053448c410c00cd4976f9bf60773a28e1d60934aabeb4006a4a248.png] 

⇒ 13A = 12B → A/B = 12/13

⇒ 14B = 15C → B/C = 15/14

⇒ A/C = (A/B) × (B/C)

⇒ A/C = (12/13) × (15/14)

⇒ A/C = 180/182

⇒ A/C = 90/91

**∴ The correct answer is 90:91.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two ratios a:b and c:d is found by multiplying the corresponding terms, resulting in (a × c) : (b × d).

Duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a:b is the ratio of their squares, expressed as a² : b².

Reciprocal Ratio

The reciprocal ratio of a:b is 1/a : 1/b, which simplifies to b:a.</p

questions.question: Find the average of -80, -20, 30, 40, and 50.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume an arbitrary mean of 0.

Sum of deviations = −80 − 20 + 30 + 40 + 50 = 20

Number of items = 5

Average = Assumed Mean + (Sum of deviations ÷ n) = 0 + (20 ÷ 5) = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Observations are −80, −20, 30, 40, and 50.

**Formula Used:** Average = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38a76f3fc9a082a9548502fafdb2217ce7655c41044e94309f8f4f2008741fe3.png] 

⇒ Sum = −80 + (−20) + 30 + 40 + 50

⇒ Sum = −100 + 120 = 20

⇒ Total number of observations (n) = 5

⇒ Average = 20 ÷ 5 = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Deviations

The algebraic sum of deviations of a set of observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero.

Combined Average

If two groups have averages x₁ and x₂ with sizes n₁ and n₂, the combined average is (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Change in Mean

If every observation is increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided by a constant 'k', the mean also changes by the same operation with 'k'.

questions.question: If the average of 16, 28, 30, x, and 34 is 30, then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the net deviation method by comparing each number with the average (30).

Deviations: (16 − 30) = −14, (28 − 30) = −2, (30 − 30) = 0, (34 − 30) = +4.

Sum of known deviations = −14 − 2 + 0 + 4 = −12.

To maintain an average of 30, the total net deviation must be 0.

Deviation of x = +12 ⇒ x = 30 + 12 = 42.

**∴ The correct answer is 42.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers = 16, 28, 30, x, 34

Total count (n) = 5

Average = 30

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e58312bda98788986f34b818a1ef9fc75b28e988b32fd5343a169546b85fec1.png] 

⇒ 30 = (16 + 28 + 30 + x + 34) ÷ 5

⇒ 30 × 5 = 108 + x

⇒ 150 = 108 + x

⇒ x = 150 − 108

⇒ x = 42

**∴ The correct answer is 42.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

It is the sum of all values divided by the total number of values. Formula: Mean = Σxᵢ ÷ n.

Property of Deviations

The sum of the deviations of a set of observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero.

Change in Average

If each observation is increased or decreased by a constant 'k', the new average also increases or decreases by 'k'.</p

questions.question: If a student scores 168 marks out of 350, what is their percentage score?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Percentage = (168 ÷ 350) × 100

Simplify by dividing both by 7: (24 ÷ 50) × 100

Percentage = 24 × 2 = 48%

**∴ The correct answer is 48%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marks obtained by the student = 168

Total marks available = 350

**Formula Used:**

Percentage Score = (Marks Obtained ÷ Total Marks) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe8894f05269753bc610746d95b3bc9ac48f8032bd829d87c5a314a4eca1e992.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Percentage = (168 ÷ 350) × 100

⇒ Percentage = 16800 ÷ 350

⇒ Percentage = 1680 ÷ 35

⇒ Percentage = 48%

**∴ The correct answer is 48%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Definition

A percentage is a number or ratio expressed as a fraction of 100. It is often denoted using the percent sign %.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

To convert a fraction to a percentage, multiply the fraction by 100. For example, 1/4 × 100 = 25%.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.</p

questions.question:
A field roller is in the shape of a cylinder whose diameter is 2.5 metres and length is 5.6 metres.

If the roller rolls at a speed of 15 revolutions per minute, then find the maximum area (in m²) that it can roll in 45 minutes.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area rolled in 1 revolution = Curved Surface Area (CSA) = π × d × h

Total Area = (π × d × h) × Speed × Time

Total Area = (22/7 × 2.5 × 5.6) × 15 × 45

Total Area = 44 × 675 = 29,700 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 29,700 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter (d) = 2.5 m ⇒ Radius (r) = 1.25 m

Length (h) = 5.6 m

Speed = 15 revolutions/minute

Time = 45 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area of Cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

Total Area Covered = CSA × Total Revolutions

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e40b1f39c61a42f60ec39f2d72694a6e37e8bebda4321191d2c5918df3db82bb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area covered in 1 revolution = π × d × h

⇒ Area = 22/7 × 2.5 × 5.6

⇒ Area = 22 × 2.5 × 0.8 = 44 m²

⇒ Total Revolutions = 15 × 45 = 675

⇒ Total Area = 44 × 675

⇒ Total Area = 29,700 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 29,700 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area of Cylinder

It is the area of the curved part only, calculated as CSA = 2 × π × r × h.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

It is the sum of CSA and the area of the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Volume of Cylinder

The capacity or space occupied by a cylinder is given by Volume = π × r² × h.</p

questions.question: Converting the decimal number 241 to the binary number system we get:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify powers of 2 less than or equal to 241: 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1.

Subtract the largest power of 2 from the number: 241 − 128 = 113; 113 − 64 = 49; 49 − 32 = 17; 17 − 16 = 1; 1 − 1 = 0.

Assign '1' to used weights (128, 64, 32, 16, 1) and '0' to unused weights (8, 4, 2).

Binary representation: 1(128) 1(64) 1(32) 1(16) 0(8) 0(4) 0(2) 1(1) → 11110001.

**∴ The correct answer is 11110001.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Decimal Number = 241

Formula Used: Successive division by 2 (Base of Binary System).

⇒ 241 ÷ 2 = 120, Remainder = 1

⇒ 120 ÷ 2 = 60, Remainder = 0

⇒ 60 ÷ 2 = 30, Remainder = 0

⇒ 30 ÷ 2 = 15, Remainder = 0

⇒ 15 ÷ 2 = 7, Remainder = 1

⇒ 7 ÷ 2 = 3, Remainder = 1

⇒ 3 ÷ 2 = 1, Remainder = 1

⇒ 1 ÷ 2 = 0, Remainder = 1

Note: The binary number is formed by reading remainders from the last division (MSB) to the first (LSB).

⇒ Binary = 11110001

**∴ The correct answer is 11110001.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Binary Number System

It is a base-2 system that uses only two digits (0 and 1). Every digit's position corresponds to a power of 2, e.g., 2ⁿ.

MSB and LSB

MSB (Most Significant Bit) is the leftmost bit having the highest weight, while LSB (Least Significant Bit) is the rightmost bit with a weight of 2⁰.

Hexadecimal Conversion

Binary numbers can be converted to Hexadecimal (Base-16) by grouping bits into sets of four from the right. Here, 1111 0001 → F1₁₆.</p

questions.question: Which of the following relationship between the sets of integers, rational numbers, and real numbers holds good?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Numbers follow a hierarchical inclusion: Natural ⊆ Whole ⊆ Integers ⊆ Rationals ⊆ Reals.

Every Integer (Z) can be expressed as a fraction Z/1, so Z is a subset of Rational numbers (Q).

The set of Real numbers (R) includes all Rational (Q) and Irrational numbers.

Thus, the nested relationship is Z ⊆ Q ⊆ R.

**∴ The correct answer is Z ⊆ Q ⊆ R.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sets Z (Integers), Q (Rational Numbers), and R (Real Numbers).

**Property:** A ⊆ B means every element of set A is contained within set B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b608a81024f893ba20589f8e55e90ea098d69db9a86a2c505cbb4757298d9f8.png] 

⇒ Integers (Z) = {..., −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, ...}

⇒ Rational Numbers (Q) = {p/q : p, q ∈ Z, q ≠ 0}

⇒ Since any integer n = n/1, every integer is a rational number ∴ Z ⊆ Q.

⇒ Real Numbers (R) consist of all points on the number line (Rational ∪ Irrational).

⇒ Since all rational numbers are part of the real number line ∴ Q ⊆ R.

⇒ Combining these: Z ⊆ Q ⊆ R.

**∴ The correct answer is Z ⊆ Q ⊆ R.**

**__Additional Information__**

Natural Numbers (N)

The set {1, 2, 3, ...} is the most basic subset of integers, denoted as N ⊆ Z.

Irrational Numbers (I)

Numbers like √2, π, and e that cannot be written as p/q. Note that Q ∩ I = ∅ and Q ∪ I = R.

Complex Numbers (C)

The set of numbers in the form a + bi, where a and b are real numbers and i = √−1. R is a subset of C (R ⊆ C).</p
